---
title: From Quarto
description: What is different from Quarto, and how to check a project before you move it.
order: 8
---

smalldocs builds the website part of Quarto. A project that uses only that part builds with either
tool. The two builds give the same pages, the same anchors and the same links.

Check a project first:

```bash
smalldocs check docs
```

The command builds the site into a temporary folder. Then it lists what smalldocs does not read:

- each option that smalldocs ignores
- each broken link
- each piece of Pandoc's Markdown that smalldocs does not read, with its file and its line

If the command finds anything, its exit code is 1.

## What smalldocs does not do

| Quarto | smalldocs |
|---|---|
| PDF, Word, slides, books, manuscripts | Websites only. A `book` is built as a website |
| Runs `{python}`, `{r}` and `{ojs}` cells | Shows the code and runs nothing. A notebook shows its saved outputs |
| Compiles `.scss` themes | Takes any Bootswatch theme and your CSS. See [Themes](themes.qmd) |
| Lua filters | Runs none. The `linkify.lua` filter is part of smalldocs |
| Grid tables, citations, cross-references (`@fig-x`) | Does not read them. Write a pipe table, and a link to the id |
| Every Pandoc extension | CommonMark, tables, footnotes, definition lists, task lists, attributes, divs, callouts, tabsets, maths, raw HTML, shortcodes |
| Algolia search, comments, analytics | A search box over `search.json`. Add the others with `include-in-header` |

## What is the same

- smalldocs merges `_quarto.yml`, `_metadata.yml` and front matter in the same order as Quarto.
- smalldocs makes the ids of headings by the rules of Pandoc. So links and anchors that were written
  for Quarto keep working.
- A link to a `.qmd`, `.md` or `.ipynb` file becomes a link to the `.html` file. A link that starts with
  `/` starts at the root of the project.
- The HTML of the page has the same classes and ids as in Quarto, such as `#quarto-sidebar`, `#TOC`,
  `.callout-note`, `.panel-tabset` and `.quarto-grid-item`. So most CSS that was written for a Quarto
  site works.
- smalldocs runs `pre-render` and `post-render` with the same environment variables as Quarto.

## Move a project

1. Run `smalldocs check`, and fix what it lists.
2. Run `smalldocs preview`. Compare each page with the page that Quarto made.
3. In the recipe that builds the site, change `quarto render` to `smalldocs render`. Change
   `quarto publish gh-pages` to `smalldocs publish gh-pages`.
4. If the project has its own `apidocs.py`, think about `smalldocs.api` instead. See
   [The API reference](api.qmd).
